title: Paying People to Give Their Time
section: 讲话 / 报道 / 讲座
transcript:
When an organisation struggles to recruit volunteers, offering a small payment may seem an obvious solution. Yet a payment can change how an activity is understood. A person who previously regarded participation as a contribution to the community may begin to assess it as a job. If the payment is very small, that comparison may not make the activity more attractive.

A social researcher discussed this possibility through a community archive project. Residents were invited to help describe old photographs. During an initial weekend, participation was unpaid. Later, some invitation letters offered a modest payment for each completed description, while others continued to emphasise the value of preserving local history. The sessions required similar amounts of time and provided the same assistance.

The payment attracted some people who had not previously considered joining. However, several experienced volunteers submitted fewer descriptions. In follow-up interviews, they said that the piece-by-piece payment made the work feel like a cheap commercial service. They also worried that careful investigation of an unfamiliar photograph would be undervalued because it took longer than a simple description.

The archive subsequently tested a different approach. It reimbursed travel expenses and offered a shared training session, while leaving the descriptive work unpaid. This arrangement addressed a practical barrier without attaching a price to each contribution. Participation improved among residents who lived farther from the archive.

The researcher did not conclude that paying volunteers is always harmful. The project involved a particular group and a task connected to local identity. The broader point was that incentives carry messages as well as financial value. Before choosing a reward, an organisation should consider both the obstacle it wants to remove and the meaning participants may attach to the offer.

questions.prompt: Why might a small payment fail to attract an existing volunteer?
options: It may make the activity seem like poorly paid employment.
It necessarily increases the required working hours.
It prevents participants from meeting other residents.
It removes all opportunities to contribute useful information.
questions.answer: It may make the activity seem like poorly paid employment.
questions.explanation: 报酬可能把公益参与转变为工作交易，而过低的计件报酬显得不值得。

questions.prompt: What concern did experienced volunteers express about payment per description?
options: It required them to write only about recent photographs.
It would make the training sessions too long.
It failed to recognise the time needed for difficult investigations.
It offered different rates to residents of different ages.
questions.answer: It failed to recognise the time needed for difficult investigations.
questions.explanation: 复杂照片需要更长调查时间，按条计费无法体现这种投入。

questions.prompt: How did reimbursing travel expenses differ from paying for each contribution?
options: It guaranteed that every resident would take part.
It removed a practical barrier without pricing the work itself.
It eliminated the need for any archive staff.
It rewarded only the fastest participants.
questions.answer: It removed a practical barrier without pricing the work itself.
questions.explanation: 报销交通费用针对参与障碍，而不为每次贡献定价。

questions.prompt: What broader lesson does the researcher draw?
options: Unpaid organisations should avoid all forms of support.
Financial rewards have the same meaning in every setting.
Experienced volunteers never respond to incentives.
The message conveyed by an incentive matters alongside its monetary value.
questions.answer: The message conveyed by an incentive matters alongside its monetary value.
questions.explanation: 激励不仅有金钱价值，还会传递关于活动意义的信息。
